description: DesalSim is a Python collection of desalination and brine-treatment process models. The developer repository documents membrane, thermal and crystallisation technologies, including reverse osmosis, nanofiltration, electrodialysis and multi-effect distillation. Models calculate quantities such as salt concentration, energy and chemical consumption, and operating costs, and can be combined into treatment configurations. These outputs support the design and comparison of water-production and resource-recovery systems. The models are not tied to one country or observation period; input chemistry, flow and operating assumptions define each application. Source code, installation instructions and examples are freely available through GitHub and PyPI under MIT. A limitation is that combining unit models does not establish their validity for a particular plant, brine composition or cost setting. The existing model-watertap offers another treatment-process modelling environment. This review read software documentation and licence metadata without installing the package or reproducing process calculations.
